title: TypeScript 7 CI causal graph
description: Deterministic map from CI checks to root causes, consequences, first fixes, and a human resilience contract.

humanResilience.title: Faith, Hope, and Love engineering layer
humanResilience.rule: This layer explains and constrains action. It never changes pass/fail status or replaces evidence.

faith.question: What do we treat as possible enough to test?
faith.global: The system can become more trustworthy through testable changes and corrected assumptions.
faith.child: We believe the robot can be fixed, so we try one careful test.

hope.question: What does a healthy future state look like?
hope.global: Every active root cause must point to a measurable green state and a next step.
hope.child: We know what green lights should look like and which box to open next.

love.question: Who or what must not be harmed while we fix the system?
love.global: Do not hide evidence, blame people, waste effort on downstream symptoms, or trade human safety for a green badge.
love.child: We repair the robot without hurting the people using it or pretending a red light is green.

execution.action: Apply the smallest root-level fix that preserves the evidence contract.
execution.feedback: Rerun the affected signals, compare immutable evidence, and revise the assumption when data disagrees.

dependency-resolution.faith: A committed dependency graph can reproduce the same reviewed toolchain on every supported runner.
dependency-resolution.hope: Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS install the same locked graph and produce comparable evidence.
dependency-resolution.love: Do not blame contributors or rerun blindly; preserve installation logs, fix the lock contract, and avoid wasting compute.

compiler-identity.faith: Compiler identity can be verified before any compatibility or performance measurement begins.
compiler-identity.hope: Every benchmark label runs the intended executable and exact version on every platform.
compiler-identity.love: Never publish a speedup from ambiguous identities; fail closed rather than tell a convincing false story.

install-lifecycle.faith: Production installation and benchmark QA can coexist as separate, explicit contracts.
install-lifecycle.hope: Production-only installation succeeds while explicit QA refuses to fake confidence when its tools are absent.
install-lifecycle.love: Do not force production users to install benchmark-only tools, and do not weaken QA merely to obtain a green check.

evidence-generation.faith: A failed evidence pipeline can be repaired and rerun deterministically.
evidence-generation.hope: All checks complete, output parity is measured, and machine-readable artifacts are preserved.
evidence-generation.love: Keep raw failures and outliers visible; do not let summary errors, retries, or formatting hide the original signal.

evidence-provenance.faith: Every published claim can be tied to immutable source, workflow, and artifact identities.
evidence-provenance.hope: A reader can trace each conclusion back to the exact commit, run, artifact, and synchronized finding.
evidence-provenance.love: Do not overstate results or let mutable documentation rewrite history after people rely on the claim.

roots.label: Dependency graph is not reproducible
roots.childExplanation: The instruction book and the Lego pieces do not match.

roots.label: The compared compilers are not the intended compilers
roots.childExplanation: Two runners may be wearing the wrong name tags, so we could time the same runner twice.

roots.label: Install and QA lifecycle contracts disagree
roots.childExplanation: The toy only works when the big repair toolbox is present.

roots.label: The evidence run did not produce trustworthy results
roots.childExplanation: The race happened, but the scoreboard is missing or shows different finishes.

roots.label: The result is not tied to one immutable source
roots.childExplanation: We know a score, but we forgot which race and which day it came from.

consequences.label: Another runner may get a different dependency graph and a different result
Performance and compatibility conclusions may compare the wrong executables
Production-only installation can fail before the package is usable
A release decision can be made from incomplete or incorrect evidence
Readers cannot prove which revision, workflow, and artifact support the claim

fixes.label: Restore package-lock.json and npm ci before investigating benchmark behavior
Repair compiler shims and verify tsc and tsc6 versions before measurement
Allow omit-dev installation while keeping explicit QA verification fail-closed
Repair the failed QA or output-parity stage and regenerate artifacts
Link immutable commits, workflow runs, artifacts, and synchronized findings

signals.label: Locked dependency installation
signals.childSymptom: The box contains different pieces than the instructions expect.

signals.label: Stable QA compiler selection
signals.childSymptom: We cannot prove which runner is TypeScript 6 and which is TypeScript 7.

signals.label: Checker-scaling compiler selection
signals.childSymptom: The checker race may use the wrong runners.

signals.label: Production-only installation
signals.childSymptom: The toy cannot be taken out of the box without the repair toolbox.

signals.label: QA verification fails closed without the toolchain
signals.childSymptom: The safety lock says everything is fine even when the measuring tools are missing.

signals.label: Stable compatibility and benchmark QA
signals.childSymptom: The race or its checks did not finish correctly.

signals.label: Checker-scaling benchmark
signals.childSymptom: The checker race did not finish or did not produce a trustworthy scoreboard.

signals.label: Normalized output parity
signals.childSymptom: The two builders produced different toys.

signals.label: Immutable evidence references
signals.childSymptom: The score points to a page that can change later.

signals.label: Findings and publication status synchronization
signals.childSymptom: Two notebooks tell different stories about the same race.

signals.label: Checker-scaling workflow attribution
signals.childSymptom: The score is attached to the wrong race.
